source: Gillon, Ducrot et al. (2025), 'First JWST thermal phase curves of temperate terrestrial exoplanets reveal no thick atmosphere around TRAPPIST-1 b and c' (arXiv:2509.02128). JWST MIRI F1500W (effective wavelength 15.1 um, width 3.1 um): the 59-hour phase curve of program 3077 (2023 November 22 to 25) fitted with the eclipses of programs 1177 and 2304. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source, their table of results, column 'Analysis #1', the nominal analysis the paper presents: the phase-curve model of Placek et al. (2014), its equation 1, with free day-side and night-side maxima and a peak offset. The paper does not say which way the offset runs; east-positive is taken, and the value is within half a sigma of zero. The radius ratio is the square root of the printed transit depth.

radiusRatio.cell: transit depth dF = 7098 +133 -149 ppm; its square root is 0.08425
radiusRatio.where: table of results, Analysis #1, planet c, transit depth

eclipseDepth.cell: A = F_c,D,max = 392 +75 -63 ppm, the day side's maximum, which the paper turns into its dayside brightness temperature
eclipseDepth.where: table of results, Analysis #1, planet c, A

model.equation: F_c/F_* = (1/2)(1 + cos(theta - delta)) F_c,D,max/F_* + (1/2)(1 + cos(theta - delta - pi)) F_c,N,max/F_* (Methods, equation 1, after Placek et al. 2014).

dayMax.where: table of results, Analysis #1, planet c, A

nightMax.where: table of results, Analysis #1, planet c, B

offsetDegreesEast.cell: peak offset delta = 10 +25 -22 deg, direction not stated
offsetDegreesEast.where: table of results, Analysis #1, planet c, peak offset

daysideK.where: table of results, Analysis #1, planet c, T_brightness,D

nightsideK.where: table of results, Analysis #1, planet c, T_brightness,N

offsetDegrees.where: table of results, Analysis #1, planet c, peak offset
